tuNotes mobile layout audit

Before & afterMultiplayer optionsCoverage & checks

Select any screenshot to enlarge it. “Before” is recreated with the pre-audit CSS (1e2feeb), using the same current app, fixtures, viewport and fonts as “After.” Screenshots are real browser captures; proposed layouts below are diagrams.

Before & after

Fixed

Saved presets broke the range-picker grid

Adding a saved preset creates two columns. The old mobile tiles still laid out icons and labels horizontally. Stacking icons above labels keeps each action inside its own tile.

Fixed

Practice controls clipped their labels

The native selector now has room for “COMING SOON.” On narrow phones, Normal and Correct Only stack their labels and checkmarks inside their own buttons. Duration and note goals retain their existing behavior.

Fixed

Option checkboxes were detached from their labels

Classroom display and keyboard accidental guidance now use aligned rows. The checkbox is 24px and its label row is at least 44px tall.

Fixed

A long preset name widened the page

An 80-character unbroken preset name is a deliberate stress fixture. Profile picker controls and saved-choice text now wrap within their available width. The active Practice heading truncates instead of consuming notation space.

Fixed

Fullscreen overlapped the wordmark

A narrower gap and a slightly smaller wordmark reserve space for the fullscreen action during play. The app title and navigation remain visible.

Also addressed: instrument shortcut spacing in single-column choosers, long chooser headings and copy-player names, saved preset menus, and wrapping profile footer actions. These are CSS changes; note selection, copying, scoring, adaptation, player order and round rules are unchanged.

Multiplayer: a larger layout decision

Not implemented

The setup mixes a player roster, three note actions, a separate fullscreen row, a large preview, and the mode selector. The primary action changes from choosing notes for everyone to starting the round, which makes the sequence harder to understand.

Screenshot evidence: current setup and play-style selector
Recommended · proposal

Keep one page; clarify the order

Players · selected player clearly markedChoose Notes — Player 1Secondary: Use these notes for everyoneCompact range previewMode + Play StyleStart round

Keep per-player ranges and copying. Use compact rows or wrapping chips so Add player stays visible. Move fullscreen beside the play controls. Show how many players still need notes.

Tradeoff: still a scrolling page, but fewer competing actions. The diagram is not an application screenshot.

Alternative · proposal

Guide setup in three steps

1 · Players2 · Notes for each player3 · Mode & Play StyleStart round

Use progress and Back/Next controls. Let players return to earlier steps.

Tradeoff: clearer classroom setup, with more navigation and decisions about drafts and incomplete player settings. Not implemented.

Two-player touch targets: fits does not mean comfortable

Side by Side and Head to Head fit through scaling. On a narrow phone, the answer targets become small. The audit verifies containment, not comfortable simultaneous touch use.

Options: recommend Pass and Play in portrait, suggest rotating for simultaneous play, or design a smaller touch keyboard. Keep format advice optional unless deciding to change which styles are allowed.

Custom editor: short screens still need scrolling

A sticky Accept/Save area could reduce scrolling, but needs a design check with nested dialogs and the on-screen keyboard. Another option is a collapsible setup preview. Neither change is included in the quick fixes.

Result layout evidence

Result cards use normal document scrolling. A long result page is not itself an overflow bug; all rows should remain readable and reachable.

Coverage & checks

Tested sizes: 320 × 667, 360 × 800, 390 × 844, 600 × 800, 768 × 1024, and 844 × 390 CSS pixels.

Checked setup in all modes; chooser home, saved presets, all clef/instrument lists at 360px, custom range, key picker, save and adaptation dialogs; player editing and copying; play styles; profile/backup options; Practice, Challenge and multiplayer results.

Gameplay checks cover five play modes, feedback, pause/resume, resizing, fullscreen, classroom display and introductions.

Checks from the completed audit use Node 24.22.1. This report capture is documentation work and does not rerun the full application suite. Browser emulation does not verify real phone keyboards, browser chrome or simultaneous touches. Intentional roster/keyboard scrolling and explicit text truncation are excluded from horizontal-overflow failures.

Reproduce the evidence

npm run build
node scripts/notes-mobile-audit-report.mjs

Use the pinned Node version. The capture script embeds fresh screenshots, checks the baseline CSS, and writes this self-contained report. Intermediate PNGs and measurements are saved under dist/validation/mobile-report/.

Regression checks: scripts/notes-mobile-layout-browser-check.mjs, scripts/notes-mode-layout-browser-check.mjs, scripts/notes-range-picker-browser-check.mjs, and scripts/notes-viewport-browser-check.mjs.

Evidence distinguishes implemented layout changes from proposals. Open this file locally to review it offline; no external fonts, scripts or images are required.
